builder_plan.scenario: Your self-hosted model spends too long generating answers token by token.
builder_plan.change: Check whether a compatible draft model and serving integration exist before renting compute.
builder_plan.baseline: The same target with speculation off, then your existing drafter if you have one.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted draft length, tokens per second, tail latency, output quality, and total GPU cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: SpecSearch: Towards Hardware-Aware Efficient Speculative Decoding
summary: SpecSearch replaces static speculative decoding configurations and manual draft-length tuning with an automated hardware-aware search that jointly optimizes decoding strategy, draft length, and precision using an analytical cost model. It requires infrastructure for multi-GPU calibration or training a specialized predictor, adding engineering complexity beyond standard inference serving. The method can fail when deploying on hardware or workloads outside the calibration distribution, or if the performance predictor mispredicts throughput on unseen architectures.
rationale: The technique demonstrates valid throughput gains for LLM inference but requires multi-GPU calibration infrastructure and specialized training that exceeds the reader's 24GB single-GPU constraint and limited cloud budget.

claims.statement: SpecSearch replaces static speculative decoding configurations and manual draft-length tuning with an automated hardware-aware search that jointly optimizes decoding strategy, draft length, and precision using an analytical cost model. It requires infrastructure for multi-GPU calibration or training a specialized predictor, adding engineering complexity beyond standard inference serving. The method can fail when deploying on hardware or workloads outside the calibration distribution, or if the performance predictor mispredicts throughput on unseen architectures.

SpecSearch achieves an average of 2.01x the throughput of autoregressive decoding and 1.36x the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs; the Jev predictor achieves 1.30x over SD without deployment-GPU calibration.
